_comment: M4 adult friendship events (Kimi C). Gate: a real friend/best_friend edge (A's envelope). 18+. All options free.

events.title: The Missed Call
events.text: My phone shows a missed call from {person:friend}, which almost never happens, and I feel the small alarm of it.

choices.label: Call back immediately
choices.outcome_text: I called my friend back immediately and we talked for an hour about nothing urgent, which is what friends are for.

choices.label: Text them later
choices.outcome_text: I sent my friend a text hours after the missed call; they said it was nothing, and I half-believed them.

events.title: The Moving Favour
events.text: {person:friend} is moving flats this weekend and has asked if I own, or could borrow, a strong back.

choices.label: Spend the day hauling boxes
choices.outcome_text: I spent Saturday hauling my friend's boxes up three flights and was repaid in pizza and lifelong credit.

choices.label: Beg off with a real excuse
choices.outcome_text: I got out of moving day with a genuine excuse, and accepted that I now owe my friend one full Saturday.

events.title: The Unfinished Argument
events.text: An old half-resolved argument with {person:friend} has surfaced again, smaller than I remembered but sharper than I expected.

choices.label: Apologise first
choices.outcome_text: I apologised to my friend first, for my half of the old argument, and felt the knot of it loosen.

choices.label: Hold my ground
choices.outcome_text: I held my ground with my friend on the old argument; I may have won the point and lost the afternoon.

events.title: The Bad Patch
events.text: {person:friend} has gone quiet and cancelled plans twice, and mutual friends say they are going through something.

choices.label: Just show up with food
choices.outcome_text: I turned up at my friend's door with food and no questions, and we sat on the floor of the kitchen until it got easier.

choices.label: Give them space
choices.outcome_text: I gave my friend their space and sent one short message saying I was here; space, it turns out, needs saying out loud.

events.title: The Almost-Lost Friend
events.text: I realised this week that {person:friend} and I have not really spoken in months, and the silence has started to feel like a shape.

choices.label: Reach out first
choices.outcome_text: I reached out first to the friend I had drifted from, and we picked up mid-sentence like the months were a commercial break.

choices.label: Wait for them
choices.outcome_text: I waited for my old friend to reach out first, and the silence between us quietly got another month older.

events.title: The Friendly Enemy
events.text: {person:friend} has beaten me at our standing game four times running and keeps a tally on the fridge like a war memorial.

choices.label: Demand a rematch
choices.outcome_text: I demanded a rematch against my friend and lost a fifth time, gloriously, to their unbearable fridge tally.

choices.label: Concede the title
choices.outcome_text: I conceded the standing game title to my friend with a speech of exactly zero grace; the tally stays.
